notes: The page is a corrected typescript headed “Théorème de Bertini et variantes.” It states a generic linear-section irreducibility theorem, a local unibranch/normal/smooth statement, a fundamental-group surjectivity corollary, a base-change remark, and the beginning of corollary 4.

These are document claims, not results verified in this run. The remark expressly says “On n'affirme pas, cependant, que (*) soit toujours surjectif (sans hypothèse de propreté sur X).” That sentence is not a declaration that the preceding proper-case statement is unproved.
No date, own page number, or stated total page count appears. The archive sheet number is 112. SGA numerals and theorem numbers are references, not dates or page counts.

The page has three mathematical displays, two handwritten marginal verbal notes, four near-vertical marginal rules and one marginal brace. There is no mathematical diagram or other pictorial drawing beyond these margin marks.

Exact unusual forms retained include unaccented Enoncé, non respé., the slash in déduit/formellement, and grave è with a mixed d/x cell in l’è…posant. The page ends at si X; no continuation is supplied.

Only ink determined choices. The mathematical role of the bound and the potentially different source of (**) prompted close inspection; no expected inequality or expected source object was substituted for the contours. The definition of the prime-to-characteristic quotient did not determine d versus x in the prose.

The overprinted remark numeral, source X/Y, middle heading cells, article cell, and d/x cell do not establish a correction chronology. They are not forcibly encoded as sequential deletions and insertions.

The (*) and (**) labels stand to the left of their displays. Local amsmath tag placement in reading.tex preserves that arrangement. Equivalent heading/emphasis macros and the absence of handwritten identity wrappers in H are not counted as discrepancies.

Input limitation: C_prior_questions.md contained two excerpts explicitly labelled scan 116. They were ignored as outside this assignment; no scan-116 images or files were opened. The parent later sent an administrative notice confirming those extraneous excerpts. No image was reopened and no reading was changed because of that notice.

All agreed words and signs were inspected in the assigned halves; only genuinely open local places were cropped. The whole and each half were viewed once. Fourteen crops were made once each and viewed once each. No OCR, recognition library, PDF text extraction, outside source, other reader record, other page, or subagent was used.
No proof verification or formal computation was performed. The checks array is intentionally empty; transcription and typewriter-cell counting are not reported as mathematical checks.
